decisions.reason: The buzzer part-selection flexibility does not change the main-board connector inventory or connector specifications.
Selecting a prototype buzzer or suitable LCSC equivalent does not alter the requirement for local decoupling capacitors.
The source decision concerns only the passive buzzer component and does not change panel controls, inputs, mappings, or mounting.
The allowance for a suitable LCSC buzzer is unrelated to the addressable-LED supply voltage, switching, or data logic.
The buzzer selection does not change standalone USB activation, LDO capacity, or the powered load scope.
The source permits an equivalent passive buzzer part but states no GPIO assignment or mapping change.
The buzzer component choice does not affect the power-source OR-ing method, sources, or selection behavior.
The buzzer part-selection decision does not change monitored rails, monitor placement, or monitoring hardware.
The source does not state that the buzzer uses or changes the switched 3.3V load circuit or its transistor topology.
The passive buzzer selection is unrelated to I2C series-resistor values, placement, or population policy.
The LCSC-equivalent allowance is explicitly about the buzzer and does not revise the LED array's selected model or part number.
The buzzer prototype choice does not change the battery-charge status indicator, connector, GPIO, or resistor configuration.
